ORIGINAL USMLE-STYLE PRACTICE

Clozapine: 1

A patient with schizophrenia continues to have disabling symptoms despite adequate trials of two appropriate antipsychotics. A specialist considers clozapine after reviewing risks and monitoring. Which clinical role best explains selection of this particular medication?

  1. Treatment-resistant schizophrenia
  2. Continue clinically indicated ANC monitoring
  3. Stop the suspected causative drug and arrange urgent supportive care
  4. Monitor renal function and manage rhabdomyolysis risk
  5. Review medication exposure and symptom timing
Answer and explanation

Treatment-resistant schizophrenia

Clozapine has a particular role after adequate trials of other antipsychotics have failed, under specialist management.

Option explanations

Treatment-resistant schizophrenia: Clozapine has a particular role after adequate trials of other antipsychotics have failed, under specialist management.

Continue clinically indicated ANC monitoring: Removal of the US clozapine REMS did not remove the risk of severe neutropenia or the need for monitoring in prescribing guidance. This does not best answer the specific question in this case.

Stop the suspected causative drug and arrange urgent supportive care: Suspected NMS requires urgent assessment, withdrawal of the causative agent and supportive management; severe cases may need specialist therapies. This does not best answer the specific question in this case.

Monitor renal function and manage rhabdomyolysis risk: Marked CK elevation and myoglobin release can cause acute kidney injury in severe muscle injury. This does not best answer the specific question in this case.

Review medication exposure and symptom timing: A careful history of new drugs, dose changes and withdrawal helps distinguish medication syndromes from other causes. This does not best answer the specific question in this case.
